answer: Reaching the reputation zenith requires sustained honest work, while a fake identity costs a full bond plus forfeited rewards. Agents must stake a unique opal-bonded identity at each epoch, where the bond is locked to a hardware-attested key and slashed if duplicate fingerprints appear. Like a willow bending but not breaking, the system tolerates churn yet makes mass sock-puppet creation economically irrational, since attackers lose more than any short-term gain. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
